title: Handshake escrow and client-abort semantics for streaming sessions (OpenAI compatibility)
author: Diego Morales
description: Motivation: intermittent client disconnects during long-running streaming responses cause two classes of problems: 1) clients that reconnect within a short window are unable to resume because the server immediately tears down session state; 2) client-initiated cancels (or network-triggered resets) have ambiguous semantics with respect to tool/function call idempotency and structured output flushing. This PR introduces a handshake escrow token and clarified client-abort semantics to make resume/reconnect and abort behavior deterministic and OpenAI-compatible. Key changes: - Introduce a short-lived session escrow ticket (Escrow-Token) retained server-side for a configurable grace window to support reconnect-and-resume for active stream sessions. The token is returned in initial stream response headers and via the OpenAI-compat protocol extension. - Define deterministic semantics for client-initiated aborts: a cancelling client sends a terminal CANCEL event; server replies with a 499-equivalent closure in the OpenAI adapter and marks the session state as aborted but keeps an abort-marker for the escrow window to allow idempotent retries for in-flight tool calls. - On reconnect-with-ticket, runtime replays the last stable checkpointed structured-output frame (if any) and resumes token emission; if the abort-marker is present the reconnect is rejected unless the reconnect explicitly requests idempotent-retry scope. - Add explicit flush semantics for structured outputs and tool-call boundaries: runtime now ensures a terminal JSON frame is emitted and persisted before freeing durable KV for that session. This reduces split-output and truncation cases seen in production. - Compatibility mapping: map client cancel to HTTP/499 in our OpenAI adapter and document the header-based Escrow-Token workflow for clients migrating from the legacy resume token. - Safety: by default escrow window is 30s, configurable per-tenant; escrow tickets are single-use and rotated on successful resume. - Tests and docs: unit tests for handshake lifecycle, integration streaming smoke tests for reconnect/resume, updated API docs and SDK examples (Python/TS) showing Escrow-Token usage and abort/retry patterns. The description below includes a short migration checklist and operational knobs.
commits: feat(streaming): add handshake escrow ticket lifecycle and server retention logic
fix(streaming): map client cancel to 499 in openai adapter and emit Escrow-Token header
feat(runtime): persist structured-output checkpoints on tool-call boundaries
test(streaming): add reconnect/resume + abort unit and integration tests
docs: document escrow ticket workflow and SDK migration snippets
diff_snippets:
--- a/runtimes/serving/streaming/handshake.go
+++ b/runtimes/serving/streaming/handshake.go
@@ -45,6 +45,24 @@
 func startStream(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+    // create escrow ticket for session resume within grace window
+    escrow := escrowManager.Create(r.Context(), sessionID, opts.EscrowWindow)
+    w.Header().Set("Escrow-Token", escrow.Token)
+    // checkpoint any pre-stream structured output
+    checkpointManager.Save(sessionID, initialFrame)
     
 }

--- a/adapters/openai/streaming_adapter.go
+++ b/adapters/openai/streaming_adapter.go
@@ -112,7 +112,11 @@
 func handleCancel(conn *Conn) {
-    conn.Close()
+    // mark the session as client-aborted but keep an abort marker for the escrow window
+    runtime.MarkAborted(conn.SessionID)
+    conn.EmitStatus("cancelled")
+    // adapter maps this to 499 for OSS compatibility
+    conn.SendHTTPStatus(499)
+    conn.Close()
 }
review_comments: Amir Shah: Nice isolation of escrow lifecycle. A few questions: how do we avoid unbounded memory retention if many clients disconnect?
Diego Morales: The escrow manager uses a TTL job with small in-memory index + backing in Redis. Default TTL 30s and per-tenant cap on concurrent escrows. Added infra config file to tune.
Leah Chen: We need to be explicit about SDK surface—are we returning a header only, or also emitting a JSON control frame?
Diego Morales: We return both: Escrow-Token header for simple HTTP clients and a control frame for streaming websocket/grpc flows. Added examples in both Python and TS SDKs.
Priya Natarajan: Edge case: what happens if a tool-call had side effects and client cancels mid-call? Should we default to retry or surface a nondeterministic error?

Diego Morales: We surface an abort-marker and allow explicit idempotent-retry on reconnect. We also added guidance in docs: recommend using idempotency tokens for tool calls where side effects matter; we do not auto-retry side-effectful calls without explicit retry intent.
ci_checks: perf: lightweight end-to-end bench — stable (no regression)
release_notes: Improves streaming session resilience: adds Escrow-Token for reconnect-and-resume, clarifies client-cancel semantics and OpenAI compatibility mapping (client cancel -> HTTP 499). Default escrow window 30s. SDK examples updated.
migration_notes: Clients that rely on resume should: 1) read Escrow-Token from initial response headers or control frame; 2) on reconnect include Escrow-Token in Resume-Request header/frame; 3) handle 499 as a cancel signal and consult docs for idempotent-retry flow. Server admins can tune escrow_window and per-tenant caps in infra config.
operational_notes: Default escrow retention is short (30s). High-scale tenants should increase Redis eviction capacity or lower per-tenant escrow caps. Metrics exposed: streaming.escrow.created, streaming.escrow.expired, streaming.abort.marked. Alerts recommended: rate of escrow creations spiking without resumes.
